title: Exclude Students with Subqueries
learning_objective: Learn how to remove students who appear in a disqualifying set.

tutorial.explanation: A subquery can build a list of students to exclude. NOT IN then keeps only rows whose student_id does not appear in that list.
tutorial.syntax: SELECT student_id FROM students WHERE student_id NOT IN (SELECT student_id FROM exams WHERE score = 100);
tutorial.mental_model: First identify the disqualified IDs. Then query the main table and filter those IDs away.

guided_example.solution_query: SELECT student_id, student_name FROM students WHERE student_id NOT IN (SELECT student_id FROM exams WHERE score = 100);
guided_example.explanation: The subquery returns students with perfect scores. The outer query removes them.

practice.prompt: Return student_id and student_name for students who took at least one exam and never scored 100.
practice.expected_query: SELECT student_id, student_name FROM students WHERE student_id IN (SELECT student_id FROM exams) AND student_id NOT IN (SELECT student_id FROM exams WHERE score = 100);

hints: Use one subquery to require exam participation.
Use another subquery to exclude score = 100.
